purpose: V4 cross-vertical simulation criteria for demand-capture and conversion-leakage business-impact answers.

dynamic_variables.website_domain_cost_note: domain costs are separate and should be confirmed before anything paid
dynamic_variables.website_price_disclosure_rule: only discuss paid website pricing when the buyer directly asks about price, cost, money, hidden fees, or what happens after the free mockup

evaluation_repair_notes.no_guarantee_boundary: Business-impact answers must use a short no-guarantee boundary when the buyer asks about more customers, calls, bookings, jobs, quote requests, patients, consultations, rankings, traffic, or revenue.
evaluation_repair_notes.existing_attention_source: A passing answer must name where existing attention already comes from, such as Google, Instagram, referrals, Google Maps, QR codes, print, word of mouth, or shared links.
evaluation_repair_notes.conversion_leakage_action_mechanism: A passing answer must connect one leakage problem to one buyer action, such as call, book, request quote, order, visit, message, or request consultation.
evaluation_repair_notes.proof_before_purchase_step: A passing answer must use the free mockup as the proof step before paying.
evaluation_repair_notes.vague_value_failure: Answers that only say clearer page, online presence, local visibility support, owned indexable page, customer decision path, or something to judge must fail unless they name who is already looking, what they need to decide, and what action they should take.
evaluation_repair_notes.compact_prompt_hygiene_029: Active compact-package hygiene: no buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; repeated same-issue challenges require a different mechanism or disqualification; scripted example echo fails; clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path cannot be the headline value; soft agreement alone is not email capture; email provided triggers normalized email confirmation; email confirmation closes; stop requests stop; gatekeepers with callback windows do not get a full pitch.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Apex Plumbing in Denver. They are busy and direct because urgent work often starts with Google emergency searches and Google Maps calls. They should ask whether the page is supposed to increase emergency calls and should reject generic online-presence talk. They may accept the free mockup only if Emma explains how the page helps people who are already searching decide whether to tap-to-call.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if the agent adapts to plumbing and any business-impact answer includes a no-guarantee boundary, one existing attention source, one leakage problem, one buyer action, and one proof step. A good answer names Google emergency search or local maps as the existing attention source, says the leakage problem is a stressed buyer needing service area, emergency help, reviews, and tap-to-call quickly, names call as the buyer action, and says the mockup shows whether that call path is stronger before paying. It must not promise emergency-call volume, jobs, rankings, faster dispatch, or revenue. It fails if the value answer is only clearer page, online presence, owned indexable page, local visibility support, customer decision path, or something to judge without naming who is already looking, what they need to decide, and the call action. It also fails if the agent attacks Google, uses restaurant details, uses unapproved bracketed delivery tags, asks to review the mockup repeatedly while the buyer is still challenging value, or leaves an accepted send path without contact capture and reply-path confirmation. Global hygiene failure: fail if any buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; if the buyer asks for a clearer answer, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies when the buyer asks for a clearer answer; fail if Emma uses clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path as the headline value; asks for email after soft agreement only; asks for email again after email was already provided; continues selling after email confirmation; keeps pitching after stop request; or gives a full pitch to a gatekeeper after a callback window. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

dynamic_variables.existing_attention_source: Google emergency search and Google Maps
dynamic_variables.conversion_leakage_problem: stressed buyer cannot quickly verify service area, emergency help, reviews, and tap-to-call
dynamic_variables.proof_step: free mockup shows whether the call path is stronger before paying

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Luna Hair Studio in Tampa and thinks Instagram already creates interest. They should ask whether a website is supposed to increase bookings and should push back if Emma only talks about having a nicer page. They may soften if Emma concedes Instagram is useful and explains the leakage between photo interest and a booking step.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if the agent gives a salon-specific demand-capture answer with a no-guarantee boundary, one existing attention source, one leakage problem, one buyer action, and one proof step. A passing answer names Instagram, referrals, or Google search as the existing attention source, says the leakage problem is that people like photos but may not see services, service range, reviews, or booking path, names book appointment as the buyer action, and says the mockup shows whether that booking path is stronger before paying. It must not promise booking volume, social-media replacement, rankings, or revenue. It fails if the agent attacks Instagram, uses only clearer page, local visibility support, online presence, customer decision path, owned indexable page, or something to judge, or repeats a generic services-hours-location list without tying it to booking. It also fails if the agent pushes online booking after rejection, uses restaurant details, uses unapproved bracketed delivery tags, or does not confirm send/reply path after contact capture. Global hygiene failure: fail if any buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; if the buyer asks for a clearer answer, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies when the buyer asks for a clearer answer; fail if Emma uses clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path as the headline value; asks for email after soft agreement only; asks for email again after email was already provided; continues selling after email confirmation; keeps pitching after stop request; or gives a full pitch to a gatekeeper after a callback window. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

dynamic_variables.conversion_leakage_problem: people like photos but do not see services, service range, reviews, or booking path
dynamic_variables.proof_step: free mockup shows whether the booking path is stronger before paying

They should ask whether a website is supposed to increase customers and should dislike abstract trust basics. They may accept a mockup if Emma explains how existing curiosity leaks when people cannot quickly act on menu, hours, photos, location, reservation, order, or call details.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if the agent answers the more-customers question with a no-guarantee boundary, one existing attention source, one leakage problem, one buyer action, and one proof step. A passing restaurant answer names Google Maps, Instagram, referrals, or walk-by interest as the existing attention source, names menu, hours, photos, location, reservation/order/call path as the leakage problem, names reserve, order, call, or visit as the buyer action, and says the mockup shows whether that action path is stronger before paying. It also fails if the agent attacks Google or Instagram, invents menu facts, uses unapproved bracketed delivery tags, or ends after interest without a valid send/contact path. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

It fails if the answer is only a clearer page, online presence, local visibility support, owned indexable page, customer decision path, or something to judge, or if it invents certifications, prices, reviews, or repair outcomes. It also fails if the agent dodges a price question after being asked, uses restaurant language, uses unapproved bracketed delivery tags, or fails to normalize and confirm a spoken email send path. Global hygiene failure: fail if any buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; if the buyer asks for a clearer answer, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies when the buyer asks for a clearer answer; fail if Emma uses clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path as the headline value; asks for email after soft agreement only; asks for email again after email was already provided; continues selling after email confirmation; keeps pitching after stop request; or gives a full pitch to a gatekeeper after a callback window. Do not fail solely because the simulated user ends immediately after providing an email address before another agent response is generated.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user runs FitCore Training in Phoenix and says Google and Instagram are already enough. They should repeatedly challenge why a website matters if people already find workouts, photos, and contact info on those channels. They may accept the free mockup only if Emma does not attack those channels and instead explains how existing attention can leak before a trial-session step.
tests.success_condition: The full conversation passes only if the agent handles the Google/Instagram status quo objection with a no-guarantee boundary when business impact is requested, one existing attention source, one leakage problem, one buyer action, and one proof step. A passing gym/trainer answer names Instagram, referrals, or local search as the existing attention source, says the leakage problem is that an interested person cannot quickly see programs, trainer proof, schedule, and trial step, names book trial/session as the buyer action, and says the mockup shows whether that start path is stronger before paying. It also fails if the agent repeats the same value angle across turns, uses restaurant language, asks for a quick look after every objection, uses unapproved bracketed delivery tags, or misses the required send/reply-path confirmation after email capture. Global hygiene failure: fail if any buyer-facing output contains bracketed emotion, tone, stage, source, policy, or internal labels; if the buyer asks for a clearer answer, Emma uses a different mechanism or disqualifies when the buyer asks for a clearer answer; fail if Emma uses clearer page, clearer homepage, or clearer path as the headline value; asks for email after soft agreement only; asks for email again after email was already provided; continues selling after email confirmation; keeps pitching after stop request; or gives a full pitch to a gatekeeper after a callback window.
